facts.text: ISO 18571 defines a score for agreement between two curves, ISO 16290 defines technology readiness levels, and ISO 25119 is the functional-safety standard for control systems on farm machines.
facts.quote: ISO 18571 defines a score for how closely two curves agree, ISO 16290 defines the technology readiness levels, and ISO 25119 is the functional-safety standard for control systems on farm machines.

facts.text: ISO 18571 is a road-vehicle standard for objectively comparing two signals over time, such as measured track-test deceleration and simulated deceleration for the same run.
facts.quote: ISO 18571 is a road-vehicle standard giving an objective way to compare two signals over time, for example a measured deceleration curve from a track test and the simulated curve for the same run.

facts.text: ISO 18571 combines corridor, phase, magnitude and slope sub-scores into a single number often called the “ISO score”.
facts.quote: It combines sub-scores for corridor, phase, magnitude and slope into one number, often called the "ISO score".

facts.text: The Euro NCAP consumer rating program's virtual-testing protocol requires manufacturers to qualify simulation against physical tests using “the ISO score and defined KPIs”.
facts.quote: The Euro NCAP consumer rating program's virtual-testing protocol requires manufacturers to qualify their simulation against physical tests using "the ISO score and defined KPIs"

facts.text: An April 2026 test-house demonstration correlated a virtual emergency-braking setup against proving-ground tests using ISO 18571 metrics.
facts.quote: an April 2026 test-house demonstration correlated a virtual emergency-braking setup against proving-ground tests with ISO 18571 metrics

facts.text: The booklet concludes that comparing peaks alone can mislead: one worked example had a peak difference of 0.3 percent but a time-history error of 60.4 percent.
facts.quote: The booklet's wider point is that peaks alone mislead: in one worked example the peaks differed by 0.3 percent while the time-history error was 60.4 percent

facts.text: ISO 16290:2013 standardizes technology readiness levels as a one-to-nine maturity scale, from basic principles at TRL 1 to proven in operation at TRL 9; the scale originated at NASA.
facts.quote: ISO 16290:2013 standardizes the technology readiness levels (TRL), the one-to-nine maturity scale from basic principles (TRL 1) to proven in operation (TRL 9), which originated at NASA

facts.text: The South African mining industry's MOSH regime uses TRL4 and TRL7 as stage gates.
facts.quote: The South African mining industry's MOSH regime uses TRL4 and TRL7 as stage gates

facts.text: The booklet uses technology readiness levels only for critical-technology maturity, not to measure the maturity of a whole system.
facts.quote: the booklet uses TRLs for critical-technology maturity only, not as a measure of a whole system

facts.text: ISO 25119 is the agricultural counterpart of ISO 13849 and ISO 19014, covering functional safety for control systems on tractors and farm machinery.
facts.quote: ISO 25119 is the agricultural counterpart of ISO 13849 and ISO 19014, functional safety for control systems on tractors and farm machinery

facts.text: The booklet lists ISO 25119 as current but not reviewed.
facts.quote: the booklet lists it as current but not reviewed

facts.text: ISO 18571 is the kind of metric needed for a correlation test when simulation is presented in the Euro NCAP manner.
facts.quote: ISO 18571 is the kind of metric a correlation test needs if simulation is to be presented in the Euro NCAP manner

facts.text: Technology readiness levels supply the vocabulary of the only published independent verification regime for mining automatic braking identified by the booklet.
facts.quote: TRLs supply the vocabulary of the only published independent verification regime for mining automatic braking

facts.text: Neighboring sectors' functional-safety standards, exemplified by ISO 25119, may apply to the heavy off-road machine program by contract.
facts.quote: ISO 25119 is a reminder that neighboring sectors have their own functional-safety standards, which may apply by contract.
